46: ## Architecture
47: 
48: **QBrainAi** is an ASP.NET Core 9 server (.NET 9.0) providing workspace-scoped context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, GraphRAG, and GitHub automation for AI agents.
49: 
50: ### Transports
51: 
52: - **HTTP REST** — Controllers at `/qbrainai/*` in `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/`
53: - **MCP Streamable HTTP** — JSON-RPC wire protocol at `/mcp-transport`
54: - **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; tools in `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`
55: 
56: ### Workspace Model
57: 
58: A single host process manages multiple workspaces. Each workspace gets its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` via `WorkspaceAppFactory` (not child processes). The primary workspace is served directly by the host. Workspace targeting uses the `X-Workspace-Path` header. Config lives in `appsettings.yaml` under `Mcp:Workspaces`. Per-instance overrides: `Mcp:Instances:{name}:*` resolved by `McpInstanceResolver`.
59: 
60: ### Search Pipeline
61: 
62: Hybrid search combining SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses results with BM25 scoring.
63: 
64: ### Storage
65: 
66: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`), with migration projects for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server. TODO items live in the configured database as the sole source of truth; `docs/Project/TODO.yaml` is a read-only projection. `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider` accepts `database` (`sqlite` is a deprecated alias; the removed `yaml` value fails fast per TR-MCP-CFG-007).
67:

69: 
70: - `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp` — main server application
71: - `QBrainAi.Services` — ingestion, context search, models
72: - `QBrainAi.Storage` — EF Core with SQLite FTS5 + HNSW vector search
73: - `QBrainAi.Cqrs` — CQRS command/query handlers
74: - `QBrainAi.McpAgent` — agent hosting & tool execution framework

210: ## QBrain.AI Claude Plugin and Hook Contract
211: 
212: Claude must treat QBrain.AI plugin and hook setup as a live runtime contract, not background documentation. On every new Claude session in this workspace, and whenever QBrain.AI behavior looks stale, incomplete, or inconsistent, perform this validation before relying on QBrain.AI workflows.
213: 
214: ### Required Startup Validation
215: 
216: 1. Read `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` from the active workspace root and use it as the current source of truth for QBrain.AI endpoint, API key, workspace path, plugin instructions, and failure-reporting rules.
217: 2. Identify the active QBrain.AI Claude plugin cache path and version from the marker file, plugin manifest, or active wrapper path. Do not assume a previously cached path is current.
218: 3. Inspect `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\plugins\cache` for stale QBrain.AI plugin entries. Delete stale `mcpserver`, `mcpserver-*`, or `mcpserver-cowork` cache entries that are not the active plugin cache path/version for this session.
219: 4. Do not delete the active plugin cache path for the current session. If unsure which path is active, stop deleting and report the ambiguity.
220: 5. Reload or rebootstrap the active QBrain.AI Claude plugin after stale cache cleanup.
221: 6. Inspect Claude active settings, including user-level and workspace/session-level settings, and verify QBrain.AI hooks are actually installed in the active settings layer. Do not accept hook files existing in the plugin package as proof that hooks are active.
222: 7. If hooks are missing or stale, install or refresh them through the supported QBrain.AI Claude plugin hook validation skill or wrapper path.
223: 8. Verify the plugin wrapper/status command works and record the exact command or tool path used.
224: 9. Verify subprocesses launched by the plugin use the workspace root as process current working directory, not the inherited user profile directory.
225: 
226: ### Required Usage Rules
227: 
228: 1. Use supported QBrain.AI plugin wrappers, hooks, skills, or MCP tools for session logging, TODOs, requirements, triage, and status checks. Do not use raw REST when a supported wrapper, hook, skill, or MCP tool exists.
229: 2. Session logging must use the supported session wrapper or MCP tools and must create, update, and complete turns through the plugin flow.
230: 3. TODO operations must use the supported TODO wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools. Do not edit TODO storage directly.
231: 4. Requirements operations must use the supported requirements wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools. Do not edit requirements storage directly.
232: 5. Triage operations must use the supported triage wrapper, workflow, or MCP tools.
233: 6. QBrain.AI failures and plugin failures discovered while doing unrelated work must always be written as a normal failsafe YAML report through the plugin failsafe flow, then submitted through triage.
234: 7. If triage submission succeeds, Claude must continue the user active task without waiting for triage research or TODO creation. If triage submission fails, stop work and notify the user. Do not invent a raw REST fallback or alternate reporting channel.
235: 8. Normal plugin execution must use PowerShell only. Bash is allowed only for installing PowerShell. Node must not be used for JSON or YAML construction.
236: 9. JSON and YAML payloads must be built from native objects and serialized. Do not handwrite YAML or JSON as fragile string literals.
237: 10. If any validation check fails, report the exact failed check, the path or command involved, and the blocked capability. Do not claim QBrain.AI compliance until the check is fixed or explicitly marked unavailable.
238: 
239: ### Minimum Validation Report
240: 
241: When asked to validate plugin or hook usage, Claude must return a concise report containing:
242: 
243: - Active workspace path.
244: - Marker file path and timestamp.
245: - Active plugin cache path and version.
246: - Stale plugin cache paths deleted.
247: - Hook settings file paths inspected.
248: - Hooks found, installed, or refreshed.
249: - Wrapper/status command used and result.
250: - Session logging validation result.
251: - TODO validation result.
252: - Requirements validation result.
253: - Triage validation result.
254: - Process current working directory validation result.
255: - Any remaining mismatch, unavailable surface, or failure.

57: ## Architecture
58: 
59: **QBrainAi** is a standalone ASP.NET Core 9 server providing context retrieval, TODO management, session logging, repository operations, and GitHub issue sync for AI agents. It exposes functionality via two transports:
60: 
61: - **HTTP REST API** — Controllers under `src/QBrainAi.Support.Mcp/Controllers/` (routes at `/qbrainai/*`).
62: - **MCP Streamable HTTP** — `app.MapMcp("/mcp-transport")` using ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.
63: - **MCP STDIO** — `--transport stdio` flag; same tools as HTTP via `McpStdio/FwhMcpTools.cs`.
64: 
65: **Workspace model**: The primary host manages multiple workspaces, each getting its own in-process Kestrel `WebApplication` (not child processes). Workspace config lives in `appsettings.json` under `Mcp:Workspaces` (not in the database). One workspace is the "primary" — served by the host process directly; others get child `WebApplication` instances via `WorkspaceAppFactory`.
66: 
67: **Search pipeline**: Hybrid search combines SQLite FTS5 full-text with HNSW vector similarity (384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX embeddings). `HybridSearchService` fuses both with BM25 scoring.
68: 
69: **Storage**: EF Core with SQLite (`McpDbContext`). TODO items use a pluggable backend — either YAML file-backed (`TodoService`) or SQLite table-backed (`SqliteTodoService`), selected via `Mcp:TodoStorage:Provider`.
70: 
71: **Multi-instance**: `McpInstanceResolver` overlays per-instance config from `Mcp:Instances:{name}` onto base `Mcp:*` settings.
72: 
73: ## Key Conventions
74: 
75: ### XML Documentation Required
76: 
77: `TreatWarningsAsErrors` and `GenerateDocumentationFile` are enabled globally in `Directory.Build.props`. All public types and members must have XML doc comments or the build fails (CS1591). Use `/// <inheritdoc />` for interface implementations. Test projects are not exempt: test classes and test methods must include XML docs that state what is being tested, what data/fixtures are used, why that data/fixtures are used, and which requirement IDs are validated.
78: 
79: ### Requirement Traceability Comments
80: 
81: All source files reference their FR/TR requirement IDs in doc comments (e.g., `/// <summary>TR-PLANNED-CORE-013: Constructor.</summary>`). When adding new functionality, reference the relevant requirement ID from `docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md` and `docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md`.
